messages.text: Got a 400k share sell block to work in a mid-cap industrial, client wants it done by the close. ADV is about 1.8M so we're ~22% of volume if we're not careful. Thinking POV 12% to start.
12% is fine for now. Spreads are 3c wide, book looks thin on the bid side. I'd hold off on the lit venues until we sniff out dark liquidity first.
What's the limit? And is the client sensitive to impact or just the benchmark? Don't want to leak this and watch it gap down on us.
Limit is 41.20, benchmark is arrival with a soft VWAP check. They're fine with a bit of slippage but not a gap. Parent order is staged in OMS now.
Parent order showing in OMS, but TradeBlotter hasn't picked up the child slices yet. Refreshing.
Normal lag on the blotter, it catches up after the first fill. Sending the first 20k into the dark pools now, IOC pings.

Ran the impact model. At 12% POV you're looking at roughly 14bps of expected slippage vs arrival. Pushing to 18% takes it to ~22bps. Volume curve is back-loaded today so the last hour carries most of it.
Stay at 12 through 2:30, then reassess. Robert, can you refresh the curve at 2:15 with the real volume?
First 20k filled in dark, avg 41.31. Got another 35k from a block crossing network at the mid. Total done 55k, 14% of parent.
Risk here. Heads up that this name is going to push the desk's single-name concentration close to the limit once the residual position clears. Derek, what's the net exposure after the sale?
It's a reduction, Owen. This block takes us from long 520k to long 120k, so exposure drops. Intraday VaR should come down as we fill.
Good, that works for me. I'll keep an eye on it as the fills come in. Ping me if you go above 20% POV.
Blotter finally synced. P&L on the slices so far is about flat vs arrival, tiny positive from the dark crosses.
2pm update: 148k done, avg 41.26, bid is stepping down a penny or two. Seeing a sizable seller on the lit side that isn't us. Might be a coincidence.
Back off to 8% for 15 minutes and let it breathe. If someone else is selling we don't want to be piling in behind them.
Agreed, throttling to 8% and leaning more on the crossing networks. Will push harder into the closing auction if the curve holds.
